solutions.check: grid rebuilt from the blog's light list (unique); every answer written into it with each crossing agreeing

clue.text: Gunmen on line claiming it's a freak

parts.note: RA is the Royal Artillery, the army's gunners

indicators.note: claiming means taking something to itself, so the railway letters hold the next piece

parts.note: RY is the abbreviation for railway, a rail line
the word it, with the 's acting as a link to the definition

explanation.surface: Armed men on a phone line or railway line are holding up something bizarre.
explanation.walkthrough: RA, the Royal Artillery, is the standard crossword gunmen; 'on' simply places them first.
explanation.definitionFit: A freak is an unusual occurrence or specimen, something seldom seen.

clue.text: Cleric doesn't finish first page of book

indicators.note: doesn't finish means the cleric's word loses its final letter

parts.note: a rector is a parish priest

explanation.surface: A clergyman stalls before getting past page one.
explanation.walkthrough: 'doesn't finish' cuts the last letter off RECTOR.
explanation.definitionFit: The right-hand page of an open book, the front of a leaf, comes first.

clue.text: Head of sport's dismissed disorder

indicators.note: head of picks out the opening letter of the sport's name
dismissed, as a batsman is, means that opening letter is sent away

parts.note: cricket's, the sport's name with its possessive

explanation.surface: The head of a sports body has been sacked.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Head of' and 'dismissed' remove C from CRICKET'S.
explanation.definitionFit: A bone-softening condition caused by vitamin D deficiency.

clue.text: It's designed to help to enlarge ultimately

definitions.text: It's designed to help to enlarge ultimately

indicators.note: designed means the letters are worked into a new arrangement
ultimately means take the final letter of enlarge

explanation.surface: A device whose design purpose is to make things bigger.
explanation.walkthrough: 'designed' rearranges TOHELPTO plus E, the last letter of enlarge ('ultimately'). The whole clue also describes the lens.
explanation.definitionFit: A camera lens that magnifies distant subjects exists to make them appear larger.

clue.text: Crook on horse making a mess

parts.note: to crook something is to bend it, as is to cock it (a wrist, an ear, a hat)
up means riding, mounted on a horse, as a jockey is said to be up

explanation.surface: A villain riding a horse causes chaos.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Crook' reads as a criminal but is the verb to bend; jockeys are 'up' on their mounts.
explanation.definitionFit: A British informal word for a botched job or blunder, a muddle.

clue.text: Group turns up in concert etc occasionally

indicators.note: turns up says the hidden letters are read backwards
in says the group sits inside the run of words that follows

parts.note: the letters run across the end of one word into the next

explanation.surface: A band appears now and then at concerts and similar events.
explanation.walkthrough: The draft lacked an indicator: 'in' signals the hiding. In a down clue 'turns up' reads the letters bottom to top.
explanation.definitionFit: A set of eight performers is a musical group.

clue.text: Top group of names doing runs in kilometres

indicators.note: in means the reordered letters go inside the kilometres abbreviation

parts.note: KM is the abbreviation for kilometres

indicators.note: runs means the letters of doing are set loose into a new order

explanation.surface: A leading team of named athletes are doing runs measured in kilometres.
explanation.walkthrough: 'runs' looks like part of the athletic picture but signals rearranging 'doing'; 'Top group of names' refers to biological taxonomy.
explanation.definitionFit: In biological classification the highest rank of named taxa, such as animals or plants.

clue.text: Arrange to be in Paris with English timber supplier

parts.note: to plan is to arrange
être is French for to be

explanation.surface: Organising a stay in Paris with an English wood merchant.
explanation.walkthrough: 'with' just joins the pieces.
explanation.definitionFit: A large tree, common in city streets, whose wood is used; a source of timber.

clue.text: Officer killed seals in Baltic …

indicators.note: seals means encloses, so the word for killed wraps round the officer

parts.note: iced is slang for murdered
COL is the abbreviation for colonel

explanation.surface: A military officer slaughtered seals in the Baltic Sea.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Baltic' is the definition, British slang for freezing; the seals are a verb, not animals. The ellipsis carries the Baltic into the next clue.
explanation.definitionFit: Baltic is informal British slang for bitterly freezing weather.

clue.text: … where resident avoids small schoolboy

indicators.note: avoids means the native of that Baltic state does without the letter for small

parts.note: following on from the Baltic in the previous clue, a resident there could be from Estonia

explanation.surface: Continuing from the Baltic: a local there steers clear of a little pupil.
explanation.walkthrough: The 'where' points back to 'Baltic' in the previous clue, giving a Baltic resident.
explanation.definitionFit: A pupil of Eton College, the famous English boys' boarding school, is called this.

clue.text: Standard question about tango floor work

parts.note: par is the standard level

indicators.note: about means the question goes round the letter for tango

parts.note: a query is a question
T is tango in the NATO phonetic alphabet

explanation.surface: A normal question about the tango's footwork on the dance floor.
explanation.walkthrough: 'floor work' suggests dance; it is woodwork laid as flooring.
explanation.definitionFit: Inlaid geometric wooden flooring is a type of floor work.

clue.text: Post Office silly to accept right idea for generator

indicators.note: to accept means to take in, so the word for silly holds the next letters

parts.note: wet means feeble or foolish in British usage
a plan is an idea or scheme

explanation.surface: Somebody at the post office foolishly takes on a proper scheme.
explanation.walkthrough: 'wet' is British for weak or foolish; it takes in R and PLAN.
explanation.definitionFit: An installation producing electricity is a generator on a large scale.

clue.text: Was attractive Scotsman missing a name?

indicators.note: missing means the Scotsman's name goes without the next two letters

parts.note: Andrew is a typical Scottish name, after St Andrew, Scotland's patron saint

explanation.surface: Was a charming fellow from Scotland lacking a name?
explanation.walkthrough: 'missing' takes A and N (name) from ANDREW.
explanation.definitionFit: To draw is to attract, as a show draws crowds; past tense matches.

clue.text: Heading west, huge saddle's dropped rope

indicators.note: in an across clue, heading west means the remaining letters are read right to left
dropped means the saddle word is let go from the word for huge

parts.note: colossal means huge
a col is a saddle, the low pass between two mountain peaks

explanation.surface: A cowboy riding west loses an enormous saddle.
explanation.walkthrough: The saddle is not for a horse but a col, a dip between mountain peaks; 'Heading west' reads the remainder right to left.
explanation.definitionFit: A cowboy's looped rope for catching cattle.

clue.text: Large ducks spotted with officer? They need tying up

parts.note: a duck is a score of zero in cricket, so two ducks are two Os
seen means spotted
DS is a detective sergeant

explanation.surface: Big ducks spotted with a police officer, who must tie them up?
explanation.walkthrough: A duck is a nought, written O.
explanation.definitionFit: Unfinished matters needing to be settled are said to need tying up.

clue.text: Slough papers cover meeting of shareholders

indicators.note: cover means the papers wrap round the meeting

parts.note: a quire is a set of 24 or 25 sheets of paper
AGM is an annual general meeting, held for shareholders

explanation.surface: Newspapers in Slough report on a company's shareholder meeting.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Slough' looks like the English town but is a bog.
explanation.definitionFit: A slough is a swamp or boggy hollow, a synonym for a mire.

clue.text: A dry conclusion by a property owner's valet

parts.note: TT means teetotal, so dry
an end is a conclusion
NT is the National Trust, Britain's great owner of historic properties

explanation.surface: A dry ending supplied by a landlord's manservant.
explanation.walkthrough: The National Trust is a British charity owning stately homes.
explanation.definitionFit: A personal servant who waits on someone is an attendant.

clue.text: Evidence of boring old empty room's incomplete

indicators.note: the 's stands for is, so the old room is set inside the following word

parts.note: read as in complete: complete means whole, the in placing the old room inside it

indicators.note: empty means the room loses everything but its outer letters

parts.note: the word room, of which only the outside letters are kept

explanation.surface: Proof that the dull old empty room is unfinished.
explanation.walkthrough: 'incomplete' does two jobs, split as 'in complete': complete gives the outer word and 'in' puts the old room, emptied to its outer letters, inside it.
explanation.definitionFit: A hole bored by a burrowing grub in wood or fruit shows where it tunnelled.

clue.text: Note about European theatre souvenir

indicators.note: about means the note goes round the next letters

parts.note: a memo is a brief written note
NT is the National Theatre in London

explanation.surface: A note about a European playhouse kept as a keepsake.
explanation.walkthrough: London's National Theatre is the usual crossword theatre.
explanation.definitionFit: A keepsake kept as a reminder of a person or event.

clue.text: What señorita displays until decorum covers it

indicators.note: covers it means the two words hold the answer within them

explanation.surface: A Spanish young lady shows modesty until it is no longer covered.
explanation.walkthrough: 'covers it' hides the letters across untIL DEcorum.
explanation.definitionFit: The wavy mark over the n in the Spanish word for a young woman.

clue.text: The French city hosting duke is disappointed

parts.note: le is French for the

indicators.note: hosting means the city takes the duke in as a guest

parts.note: a town is a city in loose sense

explanation.surface: A French city entertaining a duke is left disappointed.
explanation.walkthrough: 'hosting' puts D in TOWN.
explanation.definitionFit: Feeling disappointed is feeling let down, an idiomatic phrase.

clue.text: Hilary's one expression

definitions.meaning: Hilary is the name of the spring session at Oxford and in the law courts
a word or phrase used for something

explanation.surface: Something characteristic said by a person named Hilary.
explanation.walkthrough: Hilary looks like a person; it is the university session that runs January to March.
explanation.definitionFit: Hilary is an academic session at Oxford; a word for something is also called this.

clue.text: Rise in sea level bound to draw over 500

parts.note: a spring is a leap or bound

indicators.note: over means the draw extends across the numeral, holding it inside

parts.note: a tie is a drawn game
D is the Roman numeral for 500

explanation.surface: Leaping up to a tie in a game worth over 500 points.
explanation.walkthrough: 'over' puts TIE round D.
explanation.definitionFit: The high tide at new and full moon when the water rises furthest.

clue.text: Row round rare swimmer

indicators.note: round means the quarrel goes about the letter for rare

parts.note: a spat is a quarrel or row

explanation.surface: An argument erupts over a scarce fish.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Row' reads as rowing a boat but is a quarrel.
explanation.definitionFit: A small herring-like fish; crosswords often call any fish a swimmer.

clue.text: Lament withdrawal of eastern network

indicators.note: withdrawal of means pulling back, so the letters read in the opposite direction

parts.note: a grid is a network, as of power lines

explanation.surface: Mourning the closure of a network in the east.
explanation.walkthrough: In a down clue, 'withdrawal of' reads E plus GRID upwards.
explanation.definitionFit: A mournful song for the dead is a lament.

clue.text: Small spaces are filled by new trap

indicators.note: filled by means the spaces and the word are has the next letter put into them

parts.note: ens are small printers' spaces, half an em wide

explanation.surface: Little gaps are filled in by a fresh trap.
explanation.walkthrough: An en is a printers' space, half an em wide.
explanation.definitionFit: To catch in a snare or net is to trap.

clue.text: Salty cabbage wraps regular helpings of curry

indicators.note: wraps means the cabbage goes round the curry letters

parts.note: a savoy is a crinkly-leaved variety of cabbage

indicators.note: regular helpings means taking every other letter of the word curry

explanation.surface: Salted cabbage leaves are wrapped around portions of curry.
explanation.walkthrough: 'regular helpings of' takes the 2nd and 4th letters of curry, U and R, which go inside SAVOY.
explanation.definitionFit: Savoury food is salty or spicy rather than sweet.

clue.text: Stuck up number over in enclosure

indicators.note: in means the number and over sit inside the enclosure

parts.note: a sty is a pig's enclosure
O is the cricket abbreviation for over

explanation.surface: Someone's head is jammed in a pen, sticking up over number.
explanation.walkthrough: In cricket an over is six balls, abbreviated O.
explanation.definitionFit: Stuck-up people are haughty and condescending.

clue.text: Position volunteers between poles next to church

indicators.note: next to means the church follows on after
between means the volunteers sit inside the pair of poles

parts.note: S and N are the south and north poles
TA is the Territorial Army, Britain's volunteer reserve
CE is the Church of England

explanation.surface: Volunteers placed between poles beside a church.
explanation.walkthrough: 'between' puts TA (Territorial Army, British reserve soldiers) between S and N.
explanation.definitionFit: A stance is a position, physical or on an issue.
